prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a portrait illustration for the first of three 2011 timeline sections, titled "Snowdrops", on a dark Jackie Leven tribute website. The section date is NOT an instruction to change the age shown in the source photograph.

INPUT ROLES: Image 1 is the ORIGINAL photograph, the sole authority for Jackie Leven's identity, facial anatomy, actual apparent age, swept dark hairstyle, downward gaze, reflective pose with his hand near his mouth, open shirt collar and upright guitar neck. Image 2 is the approved SERIES STYLE reference only: follow its broad neutral-grey planes, rough broken dry-brush ink, subdued brightness and edges fading into near-black. Do not borrow image 2's face, younger age, hairstyle or pose.

Create a new vertical 4:5 head-and-upper-torso composition. Jackie is absorbed in thought, head slightly bowed, eyes lowered, with one relaxed curled hand gently resting against his mouth and chin. Preserve the exact relationship of fingers, thumb, wrist, lips and chin from image 1, with a clearly connected forearm. No exaggerated grief, tears, smile or invented gesture. Facial likeness is essential: retain his characteristic forehead and brows, eye sockets, long nose and full cheek contours, with the mouth partly concealed naturally by his hand. Do not artificially age, slim, beautify or distort him.

Keep the acoustic/electric-neutral GUITAR NECK from the photograph as a second major element beside him on the viewer's right. It rises diagonally from the lower middle toward the upper right, with a few straight string marks, suggested frets and sparse dark dot inlays, drawn with convincing straight geometry. Preserve its role as an upright instrument neck; do not turn it into a scarf, board or extra limb. Its body and headstock may remain outside the frame or lost in shadow as in the source; do not invent a detailed instrument body. Recompose the spacing for a calm upright portrait rather than copying the original wide crop. Leave dark breathing room around the head and keep the entire visible hand and wrist inside the composition.

Draw with economical rough dry-brush ink and limited neutral values, matching image 2. Broad calm light/shadow planes in face and hand, with just a few exact marks for the lowered eyes and nose. Group hair into dark masses with irregular sweeping strokes. Shirt collar is muted grey, clothing mostly charcoal and black with incomplete shoulder and sleeve strokes. Reduce the guitar neck to muted mid-grey shapes and sparse lines, no photographic wood grain or mechanical detail. Retain expressive anatomy while abstracting fine detail; it must be a drawing, not a photograph with an overlay filter.

Near-featureless anthracite #0d0f12 backdrop, faint abstract brush marks only. Remove the source's hanging ribbons, cables and all scene clutter. Strictly neutral grey/black: no yellow wood, skin colour, sepia, brown, beige or blue cast. Low-key subdued presence, no bright white face, hand, shirt or neck. Natural positive lighting, not an inverted photograph. Hair, shoulders, forearm and lower torso dissolve in broken dry-brush strokes into darkness. No smooth airbrush modelling, glossy oil impasto, repeating pebbled microtexture, vector polygons or photorealism.
One standalone 4:5 portrait, no text, logo, signature, border, flowers or memorial symbols.
